text: Correction to the packet 0120 reading note just logged: its room count was typed, not counted. Counted from the packet by grep: 60 lines in 42 rooms (not 52). The class counts (52 OUT, 1 PART, 6 held by elements, 1 by P24) were counted and stand.

OUT: joke-mode and prank play (warthunder five times, paydaytheheist, rickandmorty's premiere, samuraijack's broadcast twice, thesilphroad, twitch, wow), upvote and search-ranking stunts (4chan, clashroyale, GuildWars2, leagueoflegends twice, mls, nintendo, pokemon, popheads, startrek, titanfall), talk about other rooms' work (eve, frankocean, metalcore), the sub's own rules on its own material (anime_irl, homelab, ice_poseidon, leafs, overwatch), and in-jokes with no tie to any work. NOT: overwatch's terse replies. Two holdings differ from a room's first return and say why: zootopia's c0078 alone is held by P14 (zootopia-018 read it with c0193 as one room's need); popheads's 'This is a war' is held by P20 as the canvas's worth argued (popheads-054 held c0277's link under P04). kanye's brigading warning in canvas talk is held by P20, as schoolidolfestival-044 and vegan-056 read the host's posting rules. No NONPORTABLE line and no NEW. The rows file was drafted in the turn before this note; no row is applied yet.

Propose packet 0240 (60 lines in 42 rooms; 33 nodes, the most at T3-100 8, T3-185 6 and T3-097 5, and 2 unplaced) read whole beside each room's D3a-55 rulings and, where a node needed it, every line lifted to the node with its last ruling (new read-only helper out/_analysis/d3b_node_rulings.py; its first draft read the wrong ruling key and two Edits to it were made in one turn in parallel, against the rule; both landed and the script was then run once). OUT: April Fools styling, pranks, joke modes and kept prank features (T3-095, T3-097, T3-100), the sub's own posting rules on its own material (T3-185), and older threads and ordinary talk. PART: quebec's sub name taken from the lettering, traaaaaaannnnnnnnnns's foreseen hostility, france's thank-you pixel, paladins's false moderator claim, formula1's member who yields because the canvas is stale (P32 names strain, not staleness). Held with a reason that differs from a first return: serbia's karma call against a flag damager by P06's tracing of placers, as TheFarLeftSide-027 (no decided sanction, so not C01); quebec's plan to erase the small flag and make a large one by P02; kanye's objection to selling posters of the work by P13, as kanye-049 under G25. NEW: paladins (c0209, c0215) and portugal (c0317) each show a member who spoils the room's own work for fun and goes on when asked to stop or when it is repaired. P34 states members who turn against the room's own mark because they object to the canvas posts, and P06 states the room disowning such a placer, so neither states the griefer's act; holding it by P34 would loosen P34's subject. Accepted as a proposal, held for the notes with no move (QD3-009), beside P34. The rows file was drafted in the turn before this note and checked by a dry run (16 rejected, 42 particulars, 2 accepted); nothing is written yet.

G62 (logged before any re-check split room was read): the re-check's verdict rulings (section 4; rule 13). G60 and G60a apply, with five changes. (1) What is ruled: the 161 rooms of verdicts-recheck-D.jsonl whose two readers differ (counted by script: 145 composes against composes-with-residue, 15 cannot-tell against composes, 1 cannot-tell against composes-with-residue); where the readers agree, their verdict stands as the room's re-check verdict. (2) The model under test is the revised model the re-check readers were served (46384686...), and the fifteen candidates are part of it. (3) Organizing the revised model lacks: an act of the room's canvas organizing, shown in the item's concepts, that no element's statement or range, no arrow and no candidate states. In D3b's rulings that is an accepted correction (the statement fails without a condition the room shows), a propose line accepted as a proposal (the paladins and portugal pair), or a particular that shows canvas organizing in one room. A propose line held by an element or a candidate, a paired elaboration, a limit, the sub's own business, its April Fools play, the event as news and jokes with no tie to the work do not pass. Where a named item and a D3b ruling point apart, the item's concept words decide. (4) The ruling line is G60's, with recheck true and the revised model's hash, appended to verdicts-D.jsonl by a new helper (out/_analysis/d3b_verdict_rulings.py); the readers' lines in verdicts-recheck-D.jsonl stay as ingest compiled them. (5) Both verdict lines stand with the version on each, and no D3a-56 ruling is changed. Pages are built by out/_analysis/d3b_verdict_packet.py: figures against prior.md section 8, the verdict before, both readers' lines whole with each named item's label, and the room's re-check propose lines, corrections and particulars with their rulings whole.

G62 reading 1 (page d3b2_vp_000: the 16 splits with a cannot-tell reader, and 4chan's off-platform pair, then 49ers, aceattorney, acecombat and afip), logged before its rows. (b) Past the off-platform threshold, a reader's cannot-tell because the talk moved to a chat no longer finds residue: the chat is P23 and a canvas sub is P28 in the revised model, and the thread shows the rest (4chan, crusaderkings, paladins, pathofexile, theblackvoid). (c) Items that were residue in my D3a-56 rulings because the served model lacked them are now candidates (Bravenewbies's chat P23, crusaderkings's site K06 and developer P30, paladins's explaining P24, UNLincoln's whose-logo P24, 49ers's explaining P24, afip's tag that brings people in P25); where no reader names them they are not residue. (d) A reader's residue of the sub's own April Fools play (acecombat's HAWX policing), the event as news (aceattorney's bigger canvas) or a joke about a player (49ers's Kirk Cousins) does not pass, nor do offices (GreenEmpire's moderator posts, C01). (e) paladins's accepted proposal (R-paladins-1f38ff105273-078) is named by no reader, so it is not residue; it stands in the notes. All twenty read as composes.
